## Certified declarations

The Moore law boundary is `x ↦ xⁿ`; a boundary law `y` is filled by `x` when `xⁿ = y`, so `H₂` is
the set of units killed by the boundary and `H₁` is measured by which boundary laws are hit.
`pow_left_inj_nonneg` is the auxiliary injectivity of `n`-th powers on the nonnegative reals.

### Theorem 2.1 — parity dichotomy

- `odd_fill_existsUnique` — for odd `n` every nonzero boundary law has **exactly one** nonzero
  filling, namely `sign(y) · |y|^{1/n}`; both law-homology groups are therefore trivial;
- `even_fillable_iff` — for even `n` a nonzero boundary is fillable iff it is positive;
- `even_fill_eq_pair` — every positive boundary has exactly the two fillings `±y^{1/n}`;
- `even_units_pow_eq_one_iff` — the kernel on units is exactly `{±1}`, i.e. `H₂ ≅ {±1}`;
- `even_coker_two` — the image on units is exactly the positive units, `-1` is not in the image, and
  every unit is congruent to `1` or to `-1` modulo the image: `H₁ ≅ {±1}`.

### Theorem 3.1 and §4 — positivity repairs and erases

- `positive_fill_existsUnique` — over the positive coefficients every boundary has exactly one
  filling for every degree `n ≥ 1`, so both law-homology groups vanish;
- `positive_repairs_and_erases` — for even `n` and a negative boundary, no oriented filling exists
  while the absolute value has a unique positive filling: one coefficient change repairs the
  effectivity obstruction and erases the filling memory at once;
- `even_mixed_positive_reconstructible` — the even Moore boundary on units is neither injective nor
  surjective, the mixed phase of ULF-MATCH-1, while its positive base change has singleton fibres,
  the reconstructible phase.  The four-phase classification is therefore not invariant under
  coefficient doctrine.

# Boundary-radius normalization (Tier A scalar skeleton)

`dynamics-continent-lyapunov-avila-morales-ramis.md` §7 flags a formalizable floor behind the
boundary-modulus normalization: if a scalar coordinate has boundary radius `p^(-1/2)`, multiplying
by the inverse radius puts it on the unit circle.

This file proves exactly that scalar statement, and the diagonal specialization for `p^{-s}`. It
does not formalize Lyapunov exponents, Avila theory, Morales-Ramis theory, or the DMR consequences
in the draft.

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

noncomputable section

/-- The boundary radius attached to a positive real base `p`. -/
def boundaryRadius (p : ℝ) : ℝ := p ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))

/-- Normalize a scalar by the inverse boundary radius. -/
def boundaryUnitNormalize (p : ℝ) (x : ℂ) : ℂ := (boundaryRadius p)⁻¹ • x

/-- The boundary radius is positive for a positive base. -/
@[aesop safe]
lemma boundaryRadius_pos {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) : 0 < boundaryRadius p := by
  exact Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hp _

/-- Scaling a complex scalar by the inverse of a positive radius has unit norm exactly when the
original scalar has that radius. -/
@[aesop norm simp]
theorem norm_inv_smul_eq_one_iff {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (x : ℂ) :
    ‖(r⁻¹ : ℝ) • x‖ = 1 ↔ ‖x‖ = r := by
  have hri : 0 < r⁻¹ := inv_pos.mpr hr
  have hrne : r ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hr
  rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hri]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hm : r * (r⁻¹ * ‖x‖) = r := by
      simpa using congrArg (fun y : ℝ => r * y) h
    rw [← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel₀ hrne, one_mul] at hm
    exact hm
  · intro h
    rw [h, inv_mul_cancel₀ hrne]

/-- Boundary-radius normalization puts a scalar on the unit circle exactly when it lies on the
boundary circle of radius `p^(-1/2)`. -/
@[aesop norm simp]
theorem boundaryUnitNormalize_norm_eq_one_iff {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (x : ℂ) :
    ‖boundaryUnitNormalize p x‖ = 1 ↔ ‖x‖ = boundaryRadius p := by
  exact norm_inv_smul_eq_one_iff (boundaryRadius_pos hp) x

/-- The Frobenius weight radius `q^(w*d/2)` for a base field of size `q`,
weight `w`, and place degree `d`. -/
def functionFieldWeightRadius (q w d : ℝ) : ℝ := q ^ (w * d / 2)

/-- Normalize a Frobenius eigenvalue by its weight radius. -/
def functionFieldWeightNormalize (q w d : ℝ) (alpha : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  (functionFieldWeightRadius q w d)⁻¹ • alpha

/-- The Frobenius weight radius is positive for a positive base field size. -/
@[aesop safe]
lemma functionFieldWeightRadius_pos {q : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q) (w d : ℝ) :
    0 < functionFieldWeightRadius q w d := by
  exact Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hq _

/-- Weight normalization puts a Frobenius eigenvalue on the unit circle exactly
when the original eigenvalue lies on the weight circle. -/
@[aesop norm simp]
theorem functionFieldWeightNormalize_norm_eq_one_iff {q : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q)
    (w d : ℝ) (alpha : ℂ) :
    ‖functionFieldWeightNormalize q w d alpha‖ = 1 ↔
      ‖alpha‖ = functionFieldWeightRadius q w d := by
  exact norm_inv_smul_eq_one_iff (functionFieldWeightRadius_pos hq w d) alpha

/-- On the diagonal coordinate `p^{-s}`, boundary-radius normalization is unitary exactly on
`Re(s)=1/2`. -/
@[aesop norm simp]
theorem diagonalBoundary_unit_norm_iff (p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) (s : ℂ) :
    ‖boundaryUnitNormalize p ((p : ℂ) ^ (-s))‖ = 1 ↔ s.re = 1 / 2 := by
  rw [boundaryUnitNormalize_norm_eq_one_iff (zero_lt_one.trans hp), boundaryRadius]

/-!
# Factorization of ideals and fractional ideals of Dedekind domains

Every nonzero ideal `I` of a Dedekind domain `R` can be factored as a product `∏_v v^{n_v}` over the
maximal ideals of `R`, where the exponents `n_v` are natural numbers.

Similarly, every nonzero fractional ideal `I` of a Dedekind domain `R` can be factored as a product
`∏_v v^{n_v}` over the maximal ideals of `R`, where the exponents `n_v` are integers. We define
`FractionalIdeal.count K v I` (abbreviated as `val_v(I)` in the documentation) to be `n_v`, and we
prove some of its properties. If `I = 0`, we define `val_v(I) = 0`.

## Main definitions
- `FractionalIdeal.count` : If `I` is a nonzero fractional ideal, `a ∈ R`, and `J` is an ideal of
  `R` such that `I = a⁻¹J`, then we define `val_v(I)` as `(val_v(J) - val_v(a))`. If `I = 0`, we
  set `val_v(I) = 0`.

## Main results
- `Ideal.finite_factors` : Only finitely many maximal ideals of `R` divide a given nonzero ideal.
- `Ideal.finprod_heightOneSpectrum_factorization` : The ideal `I` equals the finprod
  `∏_v v^(val_v(I))`, where `val_v(I)` denotes the multiplicity of `v` in the factorization of `I`
  and `v` runs over the maximal ideals of `R`.
- `FractionalIdeal.finprod_heightOneSpectrum_factorization` : If `I` is a nonzero fractional ideal,
  `a ∈ R`, and `J` is an ideal of `R` such that `I = a⁻¹J`, then `I` is equal to the product
  `∏_v v^(val_v(J) - val_v(a))`.
- `FractionalIdeal.finprod_heightOneSpectrum_factorization'` : If `I` is a nonzero fractional
  ideal, then `I` is equal to the product `∏_v v^(val_v(I))`.
- `FractionalIdeal.finprod_heightOneSpectrum_factorization_principal` : For a nonzero `k = r/s ∈ K`,
  the fractional ideal `(k)` is equal to the product `∏_v v^(val_v(r) - val_v(s))`.
- `FractionalIdeal.finite_factors` : If `I ≠ 0`, then `val_v(I) = 0` for all but finitely many
  maximal ideals of `R`.
- `IsDedekindDomain.exists_sup_span_eq`: For all ideals `0 < I ≤ J`,
  there exists `a` such that `J = I + ⟨a⟩`.
- `Ideal.map_algebraMap_eq_finsetProd_pow`: if `p` is a maximal ideal, then the lift of `p`
  in an extension is the product of the primes over `p` to the power the ramification index.

## Implementation notes
Since we are only interested in the factorization of nonzero fractional ideals, we define
`val_v(0) = 0` so that every `val_v` is in `ℤ` and we can avoid having to use `WithTop ℤ`.

/-- Number of admitted powers in the complete `p`-tower at aperture `L`. -/
def ccmFirstClockPrimePowerLength (L : ℝ) (p : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  p.log ⌊Real.exp L⌋₊

/-- Fractional part of the logarithmic tower length. -/
def ccmFirstClockPrimePowerFraction (L : ℝ) (p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  L / Real.log p - ccmFirstClockPrimePowerLength L p

lemma ccmFirstClockPrimePowerFraction_nonneg
    {L : ℝ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (hpCut : p ≤ ⌊Real.exp L⌋₊) :
    0 ≤ ccmFirstClockPrimePowerFraction L p := by
  let n : ℕ := ⌊Real.exp L⌋₊
  let N : ℕ := p.log n
  have hn0 : n ≠ 0 := by
    dsimp only [n]
    exact (lt_of_lt_of_le hp.pos hpCut).ne'
  have hpowNat : p ^ N ≤ n := Nat.pow_log_le_self p hn0
  have hpowExp : ((p ^ N : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp L := by
    exact (Nat.le_floor_iff (Real.exp_pos L).le).mp
      (hpowNat.trans_eq (by rfl))
  have hpowPos : (0 : ℝ) < (p ^ N : ℕ) := by
    exact_mod_cast pow_pos hp.pos N
  have hlogLower :
      (N : ℝ) * Real.log p ≤ L := by
    have h :=
      (Real.log_le_iff_le_exp hpowPos).2 hpowExp
    rw [Nat.cast_pow, Real.log_pow] at h
    exact h
  have hlogp : 0 < Real.log p :=
    Real.log_pos (by exact_mod_cast hp.one_lt)
  rw [ccmFirstClockPrimePowerFraction,
    ccmFirstClockPrimePowerLength]
  dsimp only [N, n] at hlogLower
  exact sub_nonneg.mpr ((le_div_iff₀ hlogp).2 hlogLower)

lemma ccmFirstClockPrimePowerFraction_lt_one
    {L : ℝ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
    ccmFirstClockPrimePowerFraction L p < 1 := by
  let n : ℕ := ⌊Real.exp L⌋₊
  let N : ℕ := p.log n
  have hpowNat : n < p ^ (N + 1) := by
    simpa only [N, Nat.succ_eq_add_one] using
      Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self hp.one_lt n
  have hExpPow : Real.exp L < ((p ^ (N + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
    exact (Nat.floor_lt (Real.exp_pos L).le).mp hpowNat
  have hpowPos : (0 : ℝ) < (p ^ (N + 1) : ℕ) := by
    exact_mod_cast pow_pos hp.pos (N + 1)
  have hlogUpper :
      L < ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log p := by
    have h :=
      (Real.lt_log_iff_exp_lt hpowPos).2 hExpPow
    rw [Nat.cast_pow, Real.log_pow] at h
    exact h
  have hlogp : 0 < Real.log p :=
    Real.log_pos (by exact_mod_cast hp.one_lt)
  rw [ccmFirstClockPrimePowerFraction,
    ccmFirstClockPrimePowerLength]
  dsimp only [N, n] at hlogUpper
  have hdiv :
      L / Real.log p < (N : ℝ) + 1 := by
    apply (div_lt_iff₀ hlogp).2
    push_cast at hlogUpper
    nlinarith
  have hdiv' :
      L / Real.log p <
        (p.log ⌊Real.exp L⌋₊ : ℝ) + 1 := by
    simpa only [N, n] using hdiv
  linarith
